Confidence.description:
A probability in the closed interval [0.0, 1.0].

Confidence is reported, never inferred by a model at runtime: it comes from
how specifically a probe's response matched an interpretation rule.

DenyReason.description:
Stable, machine-readable reasons a scan request can be denied by policy.
The four wire strings below are the whole set -- agents branch on them, so
they are part of the public contract and must not be reworded without a
version bump.

Digest.description: BLAKE3 content digest of stored evidence bytes.

FoldEntry.description:
One endpoint's record, addressed by the `(target, endpoint)` pair that is
spelled the same way in every document published here.

evidence_refs.description:
Every distinct evidence digest cited for this endpoint, in
first-cited order.

observation.description: The last service identification, or `null` if nothing identified it.

rule_id.description:
The interpretation rule that produced `observation`, or `null`. This
is the name `fingerprint.explain` takes; `probe_id` is not.

state.description:
The last observed reachability, or `null` if the log contained no
`port.state` event for this endpoint. `null` is not `closed`: it means
nothing was ever observed.

target.description: The host this endpoint lives on.

Observation.description:
What a probe concluded about one endpoint. Every field beyond `service` is
optional because partial identification is normal and honest.

PortState.description:
The observed reachability of one endpoint.

`Filtered` and `Closed` are distinct on purpose: a closed port is positive
evidence that a host is up, a filtered port is evidence of a middlebox.

oneOf.description: Probed, but the response was contradictory across retries.

Terminal.description:
The three ways a scan's log can end: it completed, it failed, or it was
refused by policy.

On the wire this is an internally tagged object -- `{"outcome":
"completed" | "failed" | "denied", ...}` -- and `null` in place of the
whole object means the scan is still running or was cancelled mid-flight.
`null` never means "refused": a refused scan is `denied`, and the
difference decides whether an endpoint missing from the scan is a service
that went away or a packet that was never sent.

oneOf.description:
The scan was refused by policy and no packet was emitted under it.
`reason_code` is one of the four stable deny codes; it is not an
engine error, and retrying it without changing the authorization will
be refused again.

endpoints.description: The matching endpoints, ordered by target, then transport, then port.

hosts_up.description:
Hosts a `host.discovered` event named. Never narrowed by the filter,
which selects endpoints.

**Empty is not evidence that no host is up.** No scan emits
`host.discovered` in v0.1.

This and `plan_hash` are here because the command-line surface
reported them and this document did not. Both surfaces publish one
document, and the way to make two answers agree is not to delete a
fact from the one that had it.

plan_hash.description:
The plan the scan announced when it started, or null if it never
started. Two scans of the same plan cover the same work, which is what
makes an endpoint missing from one of them meaningful.

terminal.description:
How the scan ended, or null if it is still running or was stopped
mid-flight. A scan that was refused by policy ends `denied` and has
no endpoints because no packet was sent, not because nothing is
listening.

total_before_filter.description: How many endpoints the fold held before the filter was applied.
